steps.out: # 3D, simulations and generative pieces Use 3D when the film earns it: an object or a set as the payoff, a product, a simulation that explains. Loading Three.js, WebGPU, p5 or canvas and the seek protocol are in `../runtimes.md`. ## Deterministic by construction - Draw every frame from timeline time in the `hf-seek` listener; frames render out of order. - Simulate once at load (physics, agents, particles) into arrays, then look up the state at `t`: `render(t)` stays a pure function. Heavy setup (meshes, shader compiles, the simulation) registers a `window.__hf.buildReady` promise. - Seed every random choice; a seeded hash of the index, never `Math.random()`. ## Camera and story - One hero object beats a crowd. Fly through or into it rather than orbiting it: one dive is worth ten turns. - Cutaways, exploded views and chapters with one caption line each, plus labels with real numbers, turn a simulation into an explanation instead of eye candy. - Product UI is never tilted into 3D; only generated content tilts. ## Light and materials - Light it with a warm key, a cool rim and a dark environment with two or three soft strips; turn the environment, not the object, so highlights sweep across it; a contact shadow under the object. - Bloom eats detail: keep it to the brightest points. Glossy metal under a low light gives white streaks: roughness about 0.45 or more, environment intensity about 0.5. - One NaN pixel turns a whole frame black through bloom: clamp values that can divide by zero. ## Check it Snapshot the dive and the payoff (`../review.md`); a frame that takes too long to draw slows every render, so profile the heaviest moment once. --- name: media-use description: Get or make any media for a HyperFrames video - music, sound effects, images, icons, logos, voiceover, avatar and generated video, transcripts, cutouts, colour grades and looks - with HeyGen or free local tools, and mix placed audio. Also for footage that looks dark, flat or dull, or should be stylized or hidden. --- **Plugin installs:** Before setup or freshness commands, follow [plugin execution rules](../hyperframes/references/plugin-installation.md) when this skill is inside a HyperFrames plugin. # Media in HyperFrames Media lands as a local file in the project's `assets/` with a ledger record; renders never fetch. One verb finds or makes it: ```bash npx hyperframes media-use resolve --type --intent "" --project ``` It prints one line, `resolved → (, )`. List reusable assets first with `--candidates` and judge the fit yourself; reuse, ingest (`--from`) and adopt are in `references/resolve.md`. ## Two ways to get it | Need | HeyGen (best quality) | Free, no account | | --- | --- | --- | | Music (`bgm`) | Catalog of 10k+ tracks | Local MusicGen (`audio/references/bgm.md`) | | Sound effects (`sfx`) | | Openverse; 21 bundled offline | | Images, icons | Asset search, 75k+ | Local FLUX (mflux), if installed | | Logos (`logo`) | | theSVG, GitHub avatar, favicon; never redrawn | | Voiceover (`voice`) | HeyGen voices, voice cloning | `npx hyperframes tts` (Kokoro on device; Python 3.10+ with `pip install kokoro-onnx soundfile`) | | A presenter speaking | Avatar video (`--type video`) | Local LTX for generic clips, if installed | | Transcripts | | `npx hyperframes transcribe` (Parakeet or whisper) | | Cutouts | `heygen background-removal` | `npx hyperframes remove-background` | | Grades, LUTs, looks | | `npx hyperframes media-treatment` | **Host apps.** Inside an app that gives you its own media tools, use those first. When `HEYGEN_API_BASE` is set, the host pays for HeyGen: don't ask for the `heygen` CLI or a sign-in, and when a call is refused, relay the host's message as written and stop. **HeyGen.** Install the [`heygen` CLI](https://developers.heygen.com/cli) and sign in with `heygen auth login --oauth`: the OAuth session carries a free allowance on subscription credits; an API key (`--api-key`) bills API credits. Check setup with `npx hyperframes media-use resolve --doctor`. When a request needs HeyGen (a presenter or avatar, a HeyGen voice, catalog music) and `heygen` is missing or signed out, tell the person how to get it: the install link, `heygen auth login --oauth` for the free allowance, or an API key for credits. Then offer the free path or wait. Beyond `resolve`, the same CLI makes text-to-video (`heygen video-agent create`), avatar videos with a recorded track (`heygen video create`), cloned voices (`heygen voice clone create`), dubbing (`heygen lipsync`), translated videos (`heygen video-translate`) and short clips from a long video (`heygen ai-clipping`): recipes in `references/operations.md`. **Free.** Every tool in the free column needs no account; local models are opt-in installs (`references/setup-providers.md`). Without `heygen`, `resolve` for music, images and icons fails and says so; credit CC BY sounds (`audio/references/sfx.md`). `--local-only` skips every network provider. **Cost.** Confirm before a paid call you chose to make (an avatar video counts); one the person asked for just runs. `--provider ` pins one generator when the person names it. ## Looks on real footage Feedback that footage is dark, flat or dull, should feel retro or printed, needs a face hidden, or needs a reveal is media intent: read `references/media-treatments.md`. 6:- **The bundled 21-file library is the fallback** (`assets/sfx/` + `manifest.json`): a cue Openverse has no usable match for, and every cue once Openverse is offline or rate limited, is matched against it and the file copied into the project.
7-
8:There is no `npx hyperframes sfx` command. SFX is never generated — it is retrieved from Openverse (online) or taken from the bundled library (offline). `npx hyperframes media-use resolve --type sfx` follows the same order (`--local-only` skips Openverse).
9-
10-## Licences
11-
12-Only **CC0** and **CC BY** sounds are used: never NonCommercial, ShareAlike or NoDerivatives. Each CC BY sound is credited in the project's `assets/sfx/CREDITS.md` (title, creator, licence, source link; for `resolve`, in a `CREDITS.md` beside the sound files it saves) and its `audio_meta.sfx[]` entry carries `license` and `credit`. Tell the person to include those credits wherever the video is published.
13-
14-## Cues — request → meta
15-
16-Each line names the effects it wants: `lines[].sfx: ["whoosh", "ui click"]`. The engine flattens these into cues, resolves each, dedupes identical `(id, name)` pairs (the same effect named twice downloads/copies once), and writes `audio_meta.sfx[]`:
17-
18-```jsonc
19-{
20-  "id": "3",                       // joins the cue to the caller's model (frame / scene / segment)
21-  "name": "whoosh",
22-  "file": "assets/sfx/whoosh.mp3", // downloaded or copied, relative to project root
23-  "source": "openverse" | "local", // which route resolved it
--
36:One search per distinct effect name (20 results, `license=cc0,by`; each result's licence is checked again). The pick keeps Openverse's relevance order, prefers clips that fit a cue (15 s at most; past ~4 s ranks lower) and CC0 over CC BY when they are close. The file lands at `assets/sfx/<slug>.<ext>` and `duration_s` comes from the result. Name effects concretely (`glass shatter`, not `dramatic sound`); a vague query returns a poor match. Anonymous use allows 20 searches a minute and 200 a day: past that, the rest of the run uses the bundled library.
37-
38:## Bundled library (fallback)
39-
40-21 curated files in `assets/sfx/`, indexed by `manifest.json` — `{ file, duration, description }` per key (e.g. `whoosh`, `pop`, `click`, `chime`, `riser`, `impact-bass-1`, `glitch-1`, `typing`, …). A cue name resolves by **manifest key, file basename, or slug**, so `whoosh`, `whoosh.mp3`, or `"ui click"` (→ slug) all match. Matched files are copied into the project's `assets/sfx/`; `duration_s` comes from the manifest, so timing is known **offline** — e.g. `riser` is 10.03s, so trigger it at `climax − 10.03s`. The manifest's `description` field carries placement hints per effect; read `assets/sfx/manifest.json` for the full set and usage.
41-
42-## Rules
43-
44-- **Volume ~0.35.** SFX must sit under narration and BGM, not fight them.
45-- **No match → skip, don't fail.** A missing effect logs an anomaly and moves on; never a render blocker.
46:- **Retrieval (Openverse) or bundled library (offline) — never generation.**
47-- **One asset per distinct name.** Reuse across lines is deduped to a single search and download, many cues.
48-- **Credit CC BY sounds.** `CREDITS.md` lists them; keep it with the project.

# SPEC — "I'm flying" (Titanic bow scene, code-only)

**Format**: 1920×1080, 30 fps, 15.0 s, 2.39:1 letterbox (138 px black bars top and bottom). One scene, `compositions/bow.html`, drawn on canvas from timeline time.

**LOOK**: golden-hour Atlantic, sun at 2.6°→1.6° elevation off the starboard bow and behind the couple, so they read as rim-lit silhouettes.
- Sky: horizon #FFB26E → #E27C6C (8°) → #A8647E (16°) → #2C3460 (45°). Sun disc #FFF4D7, glow #FFBE78.
- Sea: deep #0C1C2A, sky-reflecting Fresnel, a broad glitter column under the sun, per-pixel at 960×540.
- Ship: black hull #0E0E12 with gold sheer stripe #B48C46, shaded white superstructure #B0A0A0, buff funnels #C9944A with black tops.
- Rose: plum dress #3A162C, red hair #96301A. Jack: off-white shirt #BEAF A0, brown trousers #3C3028. Rim light #FFC882.
- Type: subtitle in Noto Serif CJK SC 46 px (ZH) plus EB Garamond italic 30 px (EN), #F6EAD8. Title "TITANIC" in Playfair Display 600, 120 px, tracking 0.42em, #F1DFBD, plus 泰坦尼克号 at 34 px.
- BANNED: flat vector clip-art people, a CSS gradient pretending to be the sea, a centred sans title, bounce and elastic eases, both arms moving in unison, captions that describe the action.

**Shots (one continuous crane move)**
| t (s) | Frame |
| --- | --- |
| 0.0–4.0 | Wide, low off the port bow: the black bow cuts the sea with white water at the stem. The couple are small at the tip; Rose holds the rail and Jack holds her waist. |
| 4.0–6.4 | The camera pushes in. Rose lets go: her left arm leads by 0.3 s, a 0.35 s dip, then a 1.6 s rise to horizontal with a small overshoot. Her chin lifts. |
| 6.9–10.2 | Medium shot against the sun. Subtitle: 杰克，我在飞！ / Jack, I'm flying! Her hair and hem stream aft. |
| 8.6–10.4 | Jack's hands slide from her waist along her arms (IK keeps contact). |
| 10.2–15.0 | The camera cranes up and back to show the whole forecastle, mast and funnels. TITANIC fades in at 11.6 s. |

**Sound**: a synthesized ambience of sea wash, bow hiss and wind

# REVIEW: "I'm flying" (Titanic bow scene)

## Creative calls
- The film is one continuous crane move instead of cuts. It opens on a wide, low shot of the black bow cutting a sunset sea, pushes in to a near-frontal medium shot as Rose lets go of the rail, holds there for the line, then cranes up and back to show the whole forecastle under the title.
- Everything is drawn in code on one canvas. The sky and sea are ray-traced per pixel at 960×540: eight Gerstner-style wave normals, Fresnel sky reflection and a slope-variance sun glitter column. The ship and figures are small 3D rigs projected by hand. Rim light is the silhouette minus itself shifted away from the sun.
- Rose's arms open with a 0.35 s dip, then a 1.6 s rise with a small overshoot, left arm 0.3 s ahead of the right. Her chin lifts as they open. Jack's hands go from her waist to her arm through two-bone IK, so the contact holds.
- The format is a 2.39:1 letterbox. The bilingual subtitle sits in the lower black bar, film-style: 杰克，我在飞！ / Jack, I'm flying!
- Sound is an ambience bed of sea wash, bow hiss and wind, synthesized from filtered noise with ffmpeg. The wind swells as the arms open. No music source was available (no HeyGen sign-in, Openverse unreachable), and the original film score is copyrighted.

## Measured vs looked at
- `npx hyperframes check`: lint, runtime, layout, motion, contrast and craft all pass.
- Snapshots looked at: 0.5, 1.5, 3, 4.3–7.0 (8 frames), 7.5, 8, 9.8, 10, 10.5, 11, 11.5, 12.5, 13.5, 14.9 s, plus the phone sheet.
- The audio was measured with `hyperframes audio` but never heard.

## Weakest shot and next steps
- The faces are simple (closed eyes, smile, nose shadow), and the bodies are lofted ellipses, so up close they read as stylized rather than realistic.
- The superstructure is flat boxes. Next I would add promenade-deck tiers and bridge-wing detail, and give Rose a coat with fabric secondary motion.

steps.text:
这条 15 秒视频做好了：1920×1080，30fps，2.39:1 宽银幕遮幅。画面全部用代码在 canvas 上逐帧画出，没用任何下载的图片或视频素材。`npm run check` 全部通过，我也从渲染好的 MP4 里抽帧看过，画面正常。

**整片是一个连续的运镜：**
- **0–4 秒：** 低机位远景。夕阳下，黑色船头切开海面，船头有白浪和水花。船名 TITANIC、舷窗、四根烟囱和桅杆都在。Rose 扶着栏杆，Jack 扶着她的腰。
- **4–6.5 秒：** 镜头推近到接近正面的中景。Rose 松开栏杆，先往下一沉，再张开双臂。左臂比右臂早 0.3 秒，两臂不同步。她微微抬头，红发和裙摆被风吹向船尾。
- **7–10 秒：** 下方黑边里出现双语字幕：杰克，我在飞！/ Jack, I'm flying!
